disposition_reason: Cadmium, arsenic, lead and mercury were measured by ICP-MS in 200 drinking water samples from the Greater Gaborone supply chain; only the commercial bottled water subset is a product and is extracted.

study.design: Cross-sectional drinking water survey along the supply chain (raw and treated reservoirs, outdoor and indoor taps, commercial bottled water)
study.origin: Greater Gaborone, Botswana; bottled water brands and sources not stated
study.market: commercial bottled water, Gaborone (outlets not stated)
study.method: Microwave HNO3 digestion; ICP-MS (Agilent 7900) per CSIR method CMP33
study.lod_text: LODs determined during validation but not printed
study.qa: Field and method blanks; spike-and-recovery validation (values not printed)

findings.notes: Bottled water was about 4% of 200 samples; exact n not printed. LOD not reported.
Per-litre result kept unconverted (0.16 µg/L, ± SD). Text on p. 13 gives 0.15 ± 0.020 µg/L for the same bottled water; table value recorded.
Text p. 13: none of the bottled water contained lead or cadmium.
Per-litre result kept unconverted (0.24 µg/L, ± SD).

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Heavy metal pollution index for tap water: 0.74 (BOBS) and 33.18 (WHO)

unresolved: Tap and reservoir water results (for example indoor tap lead 1.19 ± 1.25 µg/L) are water, not products, and are not findings.
Number of bottled water samples is given only as about 4% of 200.
Arsenic in bottled water differs between Table 2 (0.16 ± 0.03) and text (0.15 ± 0.020 µg/L).
Weak proxy for flavored-carbonated-bottled-waters: plain bottled water only.
source_record_corrections: Book chapter in "Poisoning - Prevention, Diagnosis, Treatment and Poison Repurposing" (IntechOpen); chapter copyright line reads 2023.
